segment.historical_context: PHercParis4 belongs to the carbonised library recovered from the Villa of the Papyri in Herculaneum, the bulk of which transmits writings of Philodemus of Gadara — an Epicurean philosopher resident in Italy in the first century BCE who studied under Zeno of Sidon at the Athenian Garden. The recurrence of vocabulary such as ἡδονή (pleasure), ἀρετή (virtue), ψυχή (soul), φύσις (nature) is consistent with treatises on ethics, rhetoric, music, or the history of philosophy. Uncial bookhand, scriptio continua, and the absence of consistent word-division all match a luxury philosophical roll of the late Republic / early Empire.
